# twinfi

> twinfi is a command-line tool and GTK 4 desktop app for Linux that runs a Wi-Fi hotspot while the same Wi-Fi card stays connected to a Wi-Fi network (AP+STA mode). It detects what the card supports, picks a method (hostapd, NetworkManager, or a Wi-Fi Direct group on its own channel), keeps the hotspot running across suspend and channel changes, and removes everything it added when stopped. MIT licensed, Python 3.10+.

Key facts:

- Problem it solves: `nmcli device wifi hotspot` and the GNOME Settings hotspot turn the Wi-Fi card into an access point and drop the Wi-Fi connection. twinfi adds a separate virtual access-point interface instead, when the card's driver allows AP and client at the same time.
- Check a card: `twinfi detect` (reads the driver's interface combinations, like `iw phy phy0 info`).
- Start/stop: `sudo twinfi start`, `sudo twinfi stop`; start at boot: `sudo twinfi enable`; update: `sudo twinfi update`; remove completely: `sudo twinfi uninstall`.
- Methods, in order: `hostapd` (AP+STA card, hostapd installed; full client management), `nmcli` (AP+STA card), `p2p` (Wi-Fi Direct group on a second channel, used when the Wi-Fi's channel can't host a hotspot, e.g. 5 GHz DFS channels 52–144; most Intel `iwlmvm` cards), `nmcli-single` (card supports AP only; drops Wi-Fi, so used only when Wi-Fi is not connected or with `--allow-disconnect`).
- On single-channel cards (most laptop chips) the hotspot shares the Wi-Fi's channel and band.
- Requirements: NetworkManager, `iw`, `iproute2`, Python ≥ 3.10. Recommended: `hostapd`, `dnsmasq`, and one of iptables/nftables/firewalld. Optional: `jeepney` for Wi-Fi Direct on Fedora, openSUSE, Alpine, Void.
- Install: Ubuntu/Pop!_OS PPA `ppa:krotrn/apsta`; Arch pacman repo (see README); PyPI `twinfi` (`sudo pipx install --global twinfi`); `sudo ./install.sh` from source.
- Client management (hostapd mode): `twinfi clients`, disconnect, block, per-client speed limits, MAC allow-list. QR code to join: `twinfi qr`.
- Desktop app: `twinfi-gtk` (GTK 4/libadwaita) with a system tray icon (StatusNotifierItem: KDE, Xfce, Cinnamon, MATE, Budgie, LXQt, waybar; GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension); `twinfi-gtk --background` starts in the tray.
- Scripting: `status`, `detect`, `config`, `clients` and `start` accept `--json`.
- Alternative to: create_ap (archived in September 2021), linux-wifi-hotspot, manual hostapd + dnsmasq setups.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/krotrn/twinfi/blob/main/README.md): install, usage, settings, comparison with other tools, supported hardware, FAQ
- [How it works, in plain language](https://github.com/krotrn/twinfi/blob/main/docs/how-it-works.md): channels, DFS, common problems and fixes
- [5 GHz Wi-Fi](https://github.com/krotrn/twinfi/blob/main/docs/5ghz-wifi.md): why a hotspot won't start on some 5 GHz channels, and the fixes
- [Wi-Fi Direct fallback](https://github.com/krotrn/twinfi/blob/main/docs/wifi-direct.md): the `p2p` method, supported cards and distributions
- [JSON output](https://github.com/krotrn/twinfi/blob/main/docs/json-output.md): keys and exit codes for scripts
